title: Token velocity vs N‑day retention — back‑of‑napkin LTV
content:
Purpose / quick note:
- Trying to reconcile token velocity (tokens/day per active user) with N‑day retention to generate a simple LTV per cohort that we can use for microtier sizing and free credit allocations.
- Keep it intentionally conservative (bias towards underestimating revenue, overestimating cost) for runway-sensitive planning.

Assumptions (pick a baseline cohort):
- Avg revenue per paid seat (monthly) = variable depending on tier; for token-driven plan we'll convert to $/1k tokens.
- Infra cost per 1k tokens (hosted inference, mixed model mix) = $0.018 (baseline, includes avg of generation + embedding calls, KV cache hit estimated) — see infra-cost-calcs sheet for derivation (GH-PR-4220).
- Gross margin target = 70% initially (we need headroom for S&M).
- CAC for small self-serve conversion = $90 (ballpark).

Key user behaviour variables to play with:
- tokens_per_active_day (TPD) — how many tokens an engaged user consumes on days they use product
- active_days_in_30d (AD30) — number of days used in 30-day window
- conversion_rate_free_to_paid (CR) — for free trial/credits -> paid conversion
- paid_churn_monthly (CHURN) — e.g., 6% monthly => median life ~ 11–12 months

Quick formulas (B.O.E):
- monthly_tokens_per_paid_user = TPD * AD30
- revenue_per_1k = price_per_1k_tokens (we'll test $0.50, $0.30, $0.10)
- gross_margin_per_1k = price_per_1k - infra_cost_per_1k
- monthly_gross_margin_per_user = (monthly_tokens_per_paid_user / 1000) * gross_margin_per_1k
- LTV_gross_margin = monthly_gross_margin_per_user * (1 / monthly_churn)  [if churn is fraction per month]
- LTV_net = LTV_gross_margin - CAC

Scenario sketches (baseline TPD/AD30 combos):
1) Lightweight power user: TPD=200 tokens, AD30=6 
   - monthly_tokens = 1,200 tokens (1.2k)
2) Mid utility: TPD=1,200 tokens, AD30=12
   - monthly_tokens = 14,400 tokens (14.4k)
3) Heavy/power: TPD=6,000 tokens, AD30=18
   - monthly_tokens = 108,000 tokens (108k)

Test pricing points and compute LTV quickly (use infra_cost_per_1k=$0.018):
Price A: $0.50 / 1k tokens
- gross_margin_per_1k = 0.50 - 0.018 = $0.482
Price B: $0.30 / 1k tokens
- gross_margin_per_1k = 0.282
Price C: $0.12 / 1k tokens
- gross_margin_per_1k = 0.102

Pick churn = 6% monthly (0.06), CAC = $90.
Compute example LTVs: (showing formula then numbers)
- Scenario 1 (1.2k tokens/mo):
   * At $0.50: monthly_gm = 1.2 * 0.482 = $0.5784 => LTV_gm = 0.5784 / 0.06 = $9.64 => LTV_net = -$80.36 (not good)
   * At $0.30: monthly_gm = 1.2 * 0.282 = $0.3384 => LTV_gm = $5.64 => LTV_net = -$84.36
   * At $0.12: monthly_gm = 1.2 * 0.102 = $0.1224 => LTV_gm = $2.04 => LTV_net = -$87.96
- Scenario 2 (14.4k tokens/mo):
   * At $0.50: monthly_gm = 14.4 * 0.482 = $6.94 => LTV_gm = 115.6 => LTV_net = $25.6
   * At $0.30: monthly_gm = 14.4 * 0.282 = $4.06 => LTV_gm = 67.7 => LTV_net = -$22.3
   * At $0.12: monthly_gm = 14.4 * 0.102 = $1.47 => LTV_gm = 24.6 => LTV_net = -$65.4
- Scenario 3 (108k tokens/mo):
   * At $0.50: monthly_gm = 108 * 0.482 = $52.06 => LTV_gm = 867.7 => LTV_net = $777.7
   * At $0.30: monthly_gm = 108 * 0.282 = $30.46 => LTV_gm = 507.7 => LTV_net = $417.7
   * At $0.12: monthly_gm = 108 * 0.102 = $11.02 => LTV_gm = 183.7 => LTV_net = $93.7

Insights / heuristics: 
- Low token-volume users never pay back CAC unless price per 1k is very high or CAC is tiny. That implies we need either:
   * Free tier with generous credits but aggressive product hooks to increase tokens/day (drive TPD up), or
   * Very low CAC acquisition channels for low TPD cohorts (organic/community), or
   * Bundle with seat pricing for teams where tokens are additive (hide token costs).
- Mid-tier can be viable at higher per-1k price bands ($0.50) but not at commodity pricing. Heavy users are the main driver of healthy unit economics.

Experiment ideas (measure what we need):
- A: Measure real TPD distribution for new signups over first 14 days (cohort analytics query) — ticket: JIRA-PRICING-309. Target sample size 500 users.
- B: A/B test a low-friction free credit (2k tokens) vs aggressive onboarding prompt templates that push to higher TPD on day 1 (onboard flows). Metric: 7-day conversion to paid or retention.
- C: Run a small pilot price-per-1k at $0.45 for new signups with cap to observe conversion sensitivity (2-week experiment).

Packaging sketches (very rough):
- Spark (free): 4k tokens/month credit, organic community support, conversion funnel optimized.
- Flow (team starter): $20/mo + 50k tokens included, then $0.40 / 1k overage. Seat-based + tokens hybrid.
- Scale (committed/pro): $750/mo reserve with 2M tokens included, lower overage $0.08 /1k, SLA, priority support.

Why hybrids?
- Pure pay-as-you-go makes revenue lumpy and CAC payback long for low-volume users. Hybrid (seat + token bucket) moves more RU to predictable revenue and allows us to upsell token bundles.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Recompute infra_cost_per_1k with 2026 H1 kernel improvements and quantization mix (ask infra for updated profile).
- Model the effect of prefix caching: for many conversation-style products, effective tokens billed might be 20–40% lower when cache hits common system prompts. Add a "cache factor" variable.
- Decide on acceptable CAC payback window (3 months vs 12 months). For early growth aim 6–9 months maybe.
- Build small runner in python to sweep TPD/AD30/price/CAC/churn and export heatmap (next action: GH-PR-4220, Diego to take).

Random notes / heuristics for future doc:
- Consider converting large free trials into committed installments: e.g., $x prepaid for credits with 12 month expiration to improve cash flow.
- Embeddings-heavy workloads (semantic search) have different token mix — per 1k embedding units cost should be modeled separately.
- For Dedicated customers, delta cost and margin are different — we can price more aggressively. Add dedicated price table when we have dedicated infra unit costs.

Bottom line (current rough):
- If CAC ~= $90 and churn ~6% then only mid->heavy token users are LTV positive at reasonable per-1k prices. Free/low-use cohorts must be managed with either very low CAC channels or product hooks that increase token velocity.

Notes to self: save this as a working sketch, link cohort queries and run a quick sweep. Follow up with Rina on embedding unit costing for separate model.
